# Percona Operator for MySQL based on Percona Server for MySQL 1.3.0

> Percona Operator for MySQL based on Percona Server for MySQL, a Kubernetes operator that automates deployment, scaling, backups, updates and failover of MySQL clusters with group replication or asynchronous replication

Each page below is also available as markdown. For the documentation of all Percona products, see https://docs.percona.com/llms.txt.

## Overview

- [Home](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/index.md): Percona Operator for MySQL automates managing your MySQL databases on Kubernetes, making this process simple, reliable, and worry-free. Built on Percona Server for MySQL, the Operator brings…
- [Get help from Percona](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/get-help.md): Our documentation guides are packed with information, but they can’t cover everything you need to know about Percona Operator for MySQL based on Percona Server for MySQL. They also won’t cover every…

- [Features and capabilities](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/features.md): Percona Operator for MySQL is a Kubernetes-native controller that automatically manages the full lifecycle of Percona Server for MySQL clusters. The Operator offloads your teams from manual…
- [How the Operator works](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/how-it-works.md): The Percona Operator for MySQL acts as your assistant in managing databases on Kubernetes. It extends the Kubernetes API with a custom PerconaServerMySQL resource. Think of it as a blueprint that…
- [Design and architecture](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/architecture.md): Percona Operator for MySQL automates deploying and operating Percona Server for MySQL clusters on Kubernetes. This document explains what components the Operator uses and how they work together to…
- [Known limitations](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/limitations.md): This page describes known limitations of Percona Operator for MySQL based on Percona Server for MySQL. Understanding these constraints helps you plan deployments and avoid unexpected behavior.

## Quick start

- [Overview](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/quickstart.md): Ready to get started with the Percona Operator for MySQL? In this section, you will learn some basic operations, such as:
- [1. System requirements](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/System-Requirements.md): The Operator was developed and tested with the following software:
- [2. Install the Operator: Install with Helm](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/helm.md): Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes. Percona Helm charts can be found in percona/percona-helm-charts repository on Github.
- [2. Install the Operator: Install with kubectl](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/kubectl.md): A Kubernetes Operator is a special type of controller introduced to simplify complex deployments. The Operator extends the Kubernetes API with custom resources.
- [2. Install the Operator: Install with customized parameters](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/custom-install.md): You can customize the configuration of Percona Server for MySQL and install it with customized parameters.
- [3. Connect to the database](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/connect.md): In this tutorial, you will connect to the Percona Server for MySQL you deployed previously.
- [4. Insert data](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/data-insert.md): In this tutorial you will learn how to insert sample data into Percona Server for MySQL.
- [5. Make a backup](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backup-tutorial.md): In this tutorial, you will learn how to make a logical backup of your data manually. To learn more about backups, see the Backup and restore section.
- [6. Monitor the database with PMM](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/monitoring-tutorial.md): In this section you will learn how to monitor Percona Server for MySQL cluster with Percona Monitoring and Management (PMM).
- [What&rsquo;s next?](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/what-next.md): Congratulations! You’ve successfully completed the getting started guide. Your MySQL cluster is up and running. Now it’s time to prepare it for production use and learn the essential day-to-day…

## Daily operations

- [Manage users](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/users.md): MySQL user accounts within the Cluster can be divided into two different groups:
- [Connection secrets](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/connection-secrets.md): The Operator automatically creates and maintains a Kubernetes Secret for the root user that contains all connection details your applications need. This gives developers and administrators a single…
- [Backup and restore: About backups](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups.md): Backing up your database protects your data from loss and corruption, helps ensure business continuity, and lets you quickly recover if something goes wrong.
- [Backup and restore: Configure storage for backups](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-storage.md): You configure backup storage in the backup.storages subsection of your Custom Resource using the deploy/cr.yaml file.
- [Backup and restore: Incremental backups](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-incremental.md): Incremental backups copy only what changed since the previous backup in the chain. They are smaller, faster to transfer, and cheaper to keep than taking a full backup every time.
- [Backup and restore: Make scheduled backups](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-scheduled.md): Scheduled backups run automatically at times you specify. You configure them in the backup section of your Custom Resource using the deploy/cr.yaml file.
- [Backup and restore: Make on-demand backup](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-ondemand.md)
- [Backup and restore: Compressed backups](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-compressed.md): Percona Operator for MySQL uses Percona XtraBackup (PXB) to create backups. The Operator exposes this capability too, supporting compression using the zstd compression algorithm.
- [Backup and restore: Encrypted backups](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-encrypted.md): Percona Operator for MySQL uses Percona XtraBackup to create physical backups. By default, backups are unencrypted. To add an extra security layer, you can encrypt backup files before they are stored…
- [Backup and restore: Point-in-time recovery: About point-in-time recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-pitr.md): A base backup captures your data at a single moment. That is enough in many cases. If you need to undo a bad migration, recover right before someone dropped the wrong table or meet a tighter recovery…
- [Backup and restore: Point-in-time recovery: Restore with point-in-time recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-restore-pitr.md): Use this guide to restore your database up to a specific moment or a transaction target.
- [Backup and restore: Point-in-time recovery: Pause a point-in-time recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/pause-pitr.md): To debug a point-in-time recovery, pause it after the base backup is restored and before the binary logs are applied. Use this only for debugging, not for regular restores. If the recovery fails, see…
- [Backup and restore: Restore from a backup: On the same cluster](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-restore.md): You can restore from a backup as follows:
- [Backup and restore: Restore from a backup: On a new cluster](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-restore-to-new-cluster.md): You can restore from a backup as follows:
- [Backup and restore: Fine-tune backups and restores](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-fine-tune.md): When you run Percona Server for MySQL on Kubernetes, the Operator uses Percona XtraBackup to handle all backup and restore tasks. This process involves a few key binaries: xtrabackup, xbcloud, and…
- [Backup and restore: Delete the unneeded backup](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backups-delete.md): You can delete backups in the following ways:
- [Monitoring: Monitor your cluster with PMM](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/monitoring.md): In this section you will learn how to monitor Percona Server for MySQL cluster with Percona Monitoring and Management (PMM).
- [Monitoring: Monitor Kubernetes](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/monitor-kubernetes.md): Monitoring the state of the database is crucial to timely identify and react to performance issues. Percona Monitoring and Management (PMM) solution enables you to do just that.
- [Logging: Persistent logging](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/persistent-logging.md): In a distributed Kubernetes environment, it is often difficult to debug issues because container logs are tied to the lifecycle of individual Pods. If a Pod fails and restarts, its logs in stdout and…
- [Logging: Log rotation](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/logrotate.md): logrotate limits how large log files grow. Without rotation, the MySQL error log can fill the data volume.
- [Scale your cluster](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/scaling.md): One of the great advantages brought by Kubernetes platform is the ease of an application scaling. Scaling an application results in adding or removing the Pods and scheduling them to available…

## Advanced operations

- [Change replication type](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/change-replication-type.md): The Operator deploys Percona Server for MySQL with group-replication and HAProxy by default.
- [Add sidecar containers](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/sidecar.md): The Operator allows you to deploy additional (so-called sidecar) containers to the Pod. You can use this feature to run debugging tools, some specific monitoring solutions, etc.
- [Labels and annotations](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/annotations.md): Labels and annotations are used to attach additional metadata information to Kubernetes resources.
- [Configure telemetry](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/telemetry.md): The Telemetry function enables the Operator gathering and sending basic anonymous data to Percona, which helps us to determine where to focus the development and what is the uptake for each release…
- [Configure concurrent reconciliation](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/reconciliation-concurrency.md): Reconciliation is the process by which the Operator continuously compares the desired state with the actual state of the cluster. - [Check the events](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/debug-events.md): Kubernetes Events always provide a wealth of information and should always be checked while troubleshooting issues.
- [Check the logs](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/debug-logs.md): Logs provide valuable information. It makes sense to check the logs of the database Pods and the Operator Pod. Following flags are helpful for checking the logs with the kubectl logs command:
- [Troubleshoot backups and restores](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/debug-backup-restore.md): You can troubleshoot failed backups or restores by checking the status of backup and restore objects, examining the jobs that executed them, and reviewing logs from the jobs and /or the pods created…
- [Recover from a full cluster crash](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/crash-recovery.md): A full cluster crash happens when the majority of members in a cluster with Group Replication (GR) are down and the group loses quorum. Even if the primary is among the survivors, the group can’t…
- [Special files in the data directory](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/datadir-special-files.md): The mysql container of every MySQL Pod checks for several marker files in its data directory, /var/lib/mysql. When one of these files exists, the container, its probes, or the Operator change their…
- [Pause a MySQL Pod](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/pause-mysql-pod.md): Use the sleep-forever file in /var/lib/mysql when you need the MySQL container to stay up without mysqld, or when an unready Pod must report Ready so a rolling update can continue. Use the short name ps-clusterset.
- [Custom Resource reference: Backup Resource options](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-mysql/1.3.0/backup-cr.md): The PerconaServerMySQLBackup Custom Resource is used to define and manage backups for a Percona Server for MySQL cluster.
